Lucas Rivera: Heads-up  quick-eval for Orbit's LoRA merge (orbit-lora-aug1) showed a tiny but reproducible CSV/TSV formatting regression in tabular responses. Putting notes here.

Priya Shah: Oof. Can you paste before/after? downstream pipelines choke on stray delimiters.

Lucas Rivera: baseline fp16: \
```\nQ: Export order summary as TSV\nA:\norder_id	item	qty	price\n12345	Widget A	2	19.99\n```\nint4 quickpack (orbit-lora-aug1, quant int4-per-channel):\
```\nQ: Export order summary as TSV\nA:
order_id	item	qty	price
12345	Widget A	2	19.99 
```\nSee trailing space after price field and a stray non-breaking space in some lines. Quickpack metrics: TSV-strict parse rate dropped 99.8% -> 95.0% (delta 0.048). Command: `./eval_quickpack --model orbit-lora-aug1 --quant int4 --prompts tests/orbit_table_small.json`

CI Bot: CI: quick-eval orbit-lora-aug1-int4 completed  status: FAIL. Artifacts: s3://redwood-qev/orbit/aug1/int4/tsv_delta.json

Anika Muller: That could be (1) LoRA adapter adding small bias on whitespace token logits, (2) tokenizer mapping for NBSP/space got tweaked in the mapping file, or (3) quantization pushing near-zero logits across separator boundary. Any tokenizer changes in the PR?

Lucas Rivera: The PR included a small adapter to emphasize natural spacing for locale-specific thousands separators (customer requested) and we updated customers/orbit/space_map.json to include NBSP handling. Both landed together.

Priya Shah: Repro plan: 1) run token-level log: `./eval_quickpack --log-tokens --model orbit-lora-aug1 --prompts tests/orbit_table_small.json` to see final token sequence; 2) run fp16 shadow and compare token ids; 3) re-quantize with per-channel symmetric and run again. I'll kick off 1 and 3.

Anika Muller: Also run `tools/token-map-check --mapping customers/orbit/space_map.json --sample tests/orbit_table_small.json`  want to verify the NBSP entry order and whether normal space got deprioritized.

Priya Shah: Running quantize: `quantize --model orbit-lora-aug1 --scheme per-channel-sym --out /tmp/orbit_pcq`  initial per-channel symmetric int4 reduces trailing-space failures to 97.4% parse rate but still off. Posting token log excerpt.

Lucas Rivera: Token log excerpt shows baseline token ids for the price line end: `[204, 78]` (space + newline), failing int4 shows `[204, 194, 78]` where 194 corresponds to NBSP token inserted between price and newline. So tokenizer mapping introduced NBSP preference for certain numeric contexts.

Anika Muller: So root cause looks like tokenizer mapping reorder + adapter nudging NBSP probability slightly positive. Fix options: (A) reorder mapping so ASCII space has precedence for ASCII-digit contexts, (B) post-process generator to collapse NBSP to ASCII space for TSV outputs, (C) revert space_map changes for orbit until we have a robust quant profile.

Priya Shah: Quick mitigation: add a postprocess step in quickpack test harness that normalizes NBSP -> ' ' for strict TSV evaluation so we don't get false positives while we fix tokenizer. But customer-facing rollback decision should prefer mapping or adapter fixes.

CI Bot: Deployed shadow fp16 variant orbit-lora-aug1-fp16-shadow at 1771005599 for side-by-side checks.

Lucas Rivera: Action items: 1) Anika open a tiny PR reordering space_map entries to prioritize ASCII space in numeric contexts + add a unit test; 2) Priya push per-channel-sym quant artifact if regression under 2%; 3) I will add tests/orbit_table_small.json to quickpack regression list and add NBSP-normalize in CI until mapping fix lands.

Anika Muller: Opening PR now and will tag for quick review. If PR is acceptable to Orbit, we'll merge and re-run full quickpack. If not, we fall back to adapter tweak that lowers NBSP logits in generation head for TSV route only.

Priya Shah: Noted. Will update this thread with quant artifacts and post final pass/fail. :white_check_mark:
